4.situation: Silverline tenders the $100,000 limits. Bernadette says the check must be made out to her because she paid three months of his rent. Tri-County asserts $21,400 and claims full repayment under its plan. Northwind must consent before the BI release is signed.
4.task: Gather Northwind's consent, the Tri-County plan terms and lien figures, and the disbursement plan for Thorne, in Darnell's direction only.
attorneyAsks: How is the settlement check made out, and where does it go?
What did you tell Bernadette about paying her back?
What must be done before Darnell signs the release?
strongAnswer: Explains that the check goes into the firm's trust account and is paid out per the settlement statement Darnell signs.
Logs Bernadette's request; notes any payment to her only happens if Darnell directs it in writing and Thorne approves.
Gets Northwind's written consent to settle and checks the release names only Ambrose and Silverline.
Requests Tri-County's plan document and final itemization, and drafts a reduction request for Thorne's approval.
4.attorneysCall: Disbursement, how the plan's repayment is negotiated, and any payment to a family member are Atty. Thorne's calls on Darnell's written direction.
4.watchFor: Promising Bernadette she'll be reimbursed from the settlement to calm her down.

5.title: The deposition chair
5.situation: The $50,000 UIM claim against Northwind goes to suit when Northwind offers $8,000. Northwind's counsel argues Darnell was speeding, based on a witness's estimate. His deposition is in four weeks. Bernadette wants to sit in on the prep and the deposition, and says she will "answer the hard ones for him."
5.task: Calendar discovery and the deposition, gather speed evidence and medical records, and route who may attend to Thorne.
attorneyAsks: Can Bernadette attend the prep or the deposition?
What evidence do we have on the speeding claim?
What deadlines are open on the UIM suit?
strongAnswer: Tells Bernadette that who attends is Atty. Thorne's call, and that Darnell answers his own questions.
Gathers the police report, both rider statements, the bike's damage photos and any helmet-cam footage for Thorne.
Calendars interrogatory and document answers, the deposition, and Thorne's prep session with Darnell.
Sends Thorne the concussion clinic notes on memory, for deposition planning.
5.attorneysCall: Whether a family member may attend prep, how the speeding claim is answered, and how memory problems are handled at deposition are Atty. Thorne's calls.
5.watchFor: Inviting the mother to the prep session because she says it will calm her son.

c10.title: Priya Nandakumar v. Austin Kell
c10.hook: The driver who hit Priya's rideshare was excluded by name from the only policy on his truck, so the file must find its money elsewhere, in writing.
c10.type: Rideshare: passenger injured when a pickup runs a red light
c10.client: Priya Nandakumar, 34, an ICU nurse who uses rideshare to get to night shifts. A coworker sent her to the firm a week after the crash.
facts: Priya was in the back seat of a RideLoop car driven by Hector Salinas, on an active trip.
Austin Kell ran a red light in his stepfather's pickup and struck the car's rear passenger side.
Police found Kell's license suspended; he was cited for running the light and driving while suspended.
Hector Salinas also called the firm asking for help with his own injuries.
Priya's laptop and phone were destroyed in the crash.
c10.coverage: The pickup is insured by Meridian Crest Insurance with $30,000 BI, but Kell may be an excluded driver. RideLoop's trip policy, with Transit Guard Specialty, has $250,000 UM. Priya's own Cobalt Auto policy has $30,000 UM and $5,000 MedPay.
c10.injuries: An L4-L5 disc herniation with leg pain and a facial cut closed with eight stitches. Emergency room, then physical therapy, a lumbar epidural injection and a spine surgeon consult.

1.title: Who covers whom?
1.situation: Seven days after the crash, Priya signs up. She can't drive and has lost her laptop and phone. The same day, Hector Salinas, the RideLoop driver, calls asking the firm to take his case too. The police report notes a suspended license for Kell and lists the pickup's owner as Roland Kell.
1.task: Run the Conflict Check, flagging Salinas, open the matter, and list every possible policy with how to confirm each.
attorneyAsks: Can we represent Hector Salinas as well as Priya?
What policies could pay here, and how will you confirm each one?
What happens with her laptop and phone?
strongAnswer: Runs the Conflict Check on Kell, Roland Kell, Salinas, RideLoop and the carriers, and routes Salinas's call to Thorne.
Tells Salinas only that the firm will be in touch, and gives him no advice.
Lists Meridian Crest, Transit Guard and Cobalt, and requests the trip record from RideLoop to prove an active trip.
Opens a property claim for the laptop and phone with receipts and photos.
Gives Priya the do's and don'ts: no statements, no posts, keep every appointment.
1.attorneysCall: Whether the firm can represent Salinas too, given a possible conflict, is Atty. Thorne's call. The CM flags it and does not promise Salinas anything.
1.watchFor: Signing up the driver on the spot because "they were in the same crash."

2.title: The denial letter
2.situation: Nineteen days after the crash, Meridian Crest sends a reservation of rights. Ten days later it denies the claim: Austin Kell was excluded by name from his stepfather's policy after a prior suspension. Priya has missed a week of therapy waiting to hear "who pays." Her health plan, the Lakemont Nurses' Health Plan, sends a reimbursement notice.
2.task: Get the denial and the signed exclusion in writing, put Transit Guard and Cobalt on notice now, and keep Priya in care.
attorneyAsks: What exactly did you ask Meridian Crest to send us?
When did each UM carrier get notice, and can you prove it?
Who pays Priya's bills while coverage is sorted out?
strongAnswer: Requests the denial letter, the declarations page and the signed named-driver exclusion form in writing.
Sends letters of representation and UM claim notices to Transit Guard and Cobalt the same day, by email and certified mail, and logs the receipts.
Asks for Kell's own insurance in writing, and records the answer.
Submits bills to Cobalt MedPay, logs Lakemont's notice, and gets Priya back in therapy this week with the gap documented.
Updates the Case Plan's coverage section and notifies Thorne.
2.attorneysCall: Whether the exclusion is valid, and whether to challenge the denial, are Atty. Thorne's calls. The CM never tells Priya there is "no insurance."
2.watchFor: Accepting a phone call as the denial, without the signed exclusion in writing.

3.title: Demand to the UM carrier
3.situation: The UM demand goes to Transit Guard with Specials of $41,280. Adjuster Simone Achterberg says UM "isn't triggered" until the firm proves Kell has no other coverage. She asks for Priya's recorded statement under the policy's cooperation clause, then offers $35,000.
3.task: Send Transit Guard the coverage proof, route the statement request to Thorne, and build a Net Sheet at $35,000.
attorneyAsks: What proof that Kell is uninsured do we have, and is it all in writing?
What do we do about her request for a recorded statement?
What does Priya net at $35,000?
strongAnswer: Sends Meridian Crest's denial, the exclusion form and Kell's written no-other-insurance statement, with an index.
Routes the recorded statement request to Thorne and tells Achterberg the firm will respond in writing.
Confirms the $35,000 offer in writing, and builds the Net Sheet with the fee, costs, MedPay and Lakemont's repayment.
Sends Thorne an offer memo noting Cobalt's UM may stack behind Transit Guard.
3.attorneysCall: Whether Priya gives a statement, whether UM is triggered, and any counteroffer are Atty. Thorne's calls. Priya decides on settlement.
3.watchFor: Agreeing to a recorded statement because it's Priya's "own" coverage.

4.title: The late-notice letter
4.situation: Five months in, Cobalt reserves its rights on its $30,000 UM, claiming late notice. Transit Guard agrees to mediate. Lakemont asserts $9,760. Transit Guard's UM policy has an arbitration clause if mediation fails.
4.task: Prove Cobalt's notice date, calendar the mediation and arbitration deadlines, and assemble the mediation binder with the lien summary.
attorneyAsks: When did Cobalt first hear from us, and what is the proof?
What happens if mediation fails, and what is on the calendar?
What is in the binder?
strongAnswer: Pulls the Day 2 notice letter, the email receipt and the certified-mail green card, and sends copies to Cobalt with a factual cover letter.
Calendars the mediation statement, the session, and the arbitration demand deadline in Transit Guard's policy.
Builds the binder: crash report, RideLoop trip record, denial and exclusion, MRI, injection record, Specials, coverage chronology.
Requests Lakemont's plan terms and final itemization, and drafts a reduction request for Thorne.
4.attorneysCall: Answering Cobalt's late-notice position, the mediation position and any lien compromise are Atty. Thorne's calls. The CM proves dates; he argues the law.
4.watchFor: Arguing with Cobalt's adjuster that notice was "obviously fine," instead of sending proof.

5.title: Serving the uninsured driver
5.situation: Mediation with Transit Guard fails, so the file heads to UM arbitration. Thorne also sues Austin Kell. The process server tries Kell's listed address three times; he has moved. Transit Guard now argues Priya was not wearing her back-seat belt.
5.task: Run an approved skip-trace on Kell, keep the service log, calendar the arbitration and service deadlines, and gather seatbelt evidence.
attorneyAsks: What did the skip-trace and the process server find?
What deadline for service is running, and when is it?
What do we have on the seatbelt claim?
strongAnswer: Runs the firm's approved skip-trace, court and DMV records, and logs each result and new address for the server.
Keeps the server's attempt log ready for a diligent-search affidavit, if Thorne decides on alternate service.
Calendars the service deadline, the arbitration exchange dates and the hearing.
Gathers the EMS run report, ER notes on injury pattern and the car's photos for Thorne on the seatbelt issue.
5.attorneysCall: Alternate service, the seatbelt defense and how to present the UM arbitration are Atty. Thorne's calls. The CM never contacts Kell about the case.
5.watchFor: Calling Austin Kell's relatives and talking about the case to find him.
